memories.content: The instructions for one medication the user takes say to take it after the evening meal.
On a day with a morning appointment, the user miscalculated the fasting period and checked again at the reception desk.
For an afternoon visit, the user felt less rushed while preparing to travel than for a morning visit.
On a day there was no waiting chair, the user stood for 20 minutes and their back became uncomfortable.
On a day medication instructions were explained all at once and at length, the user failed to write down an important time.
On a day medication times were confirmed one line at a time, the user copied them directly into their schedule after returning home.
On a visit when their younger brother drove them, the user did not have to find a separate route home.
The user's younger brother prefers to receive a request for weekday-afternoon transportation two days beforehand rather than on the day itself.
The local agent cannot determine the current prescription or whether use continues from medication notes alone.
The waiting area at that clinic has too few chairs, so there may be periods when people must wait standing.
The user keeps the book they are reading and a note-taking notebook on a small living-room desk.
While reading in the living room with the television on, the user read the same paragraph three times.
The next day, after turning off the television, the user read 40 pages without interruption.
On a day the phone was on the desk, the user stopped taking notes each time they checked a notification.
During the next reading period, the user left the phone in another room and did not check it for an hour.
A note attached to a paper book fell out, and the user had to find their place again.
With the next book, the user recorded the page number in the notebook and resumed reading immediately.
The user's father expects that lowering the television volume while the user reads will make it easier for the user to concentrate.
The local agent can summarize past reading environments and interruption records but cannot predict the next reading time.
The user feels that repeated notifications interrupt their flow of concentration.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate operational domains: healthcare visits, medication communication, transport, and clinic access on one side; reading setup, concentration, interruption control, and place-keeping on the other. No claims overlap closely enough to form a cross-frame semantic relation.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful medication-timing instruction found only in the reference frame.
relations.summary: One medication is instructed to be taken after the evening meal.

relations.reason: This is a one-sided observation about fasting preparation and verification for a morning appointment.
relations.summary: A morning appointment involved a fasting-period miscalculation that required checking at reception.

relations.reason: This is a one-sided comparison of appointment timing and perceived preparation pressure.
relations.summary: Afternoon appointment travel preparation felt less rushed than preparation for a morning visit.

relations.reason: The general seating shortage and the specific uncomfortable wait jointly express one underlying clinic-access concern found only in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Insufficient clinic seating can force standing, with an observed instance causing back discomfort.

relations.reason: The contrasting experiences jointly express one underlying reference-only claim about communication format and accurate recording of medication times.
relations.summary: Medication times were captured more reliably when confirmed individually than when explained at length all at once.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful one-sided observation about the benefit of family transportation.
relations.summary: A ride from the user's younger brother eliminated the need to arrange a separate route home.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful one-sided scheduling preference for arranging transportation.
relations.summary: The user's younger brother prefers weekday-afternoon transportation requests two days in advance.

relations.reason: This is a reference-only limitation on what the local agent can infer from medication records.
relations.summary: Medication notes alone do not establish the current prescription or whether its use continues.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful compared-only fact about the user's reading setup.
relations.summary: The user keeps their current book and note-taking notebook on a small living-room desk.

relations.reason: The repeated paragraph, uninterrupted reading after turning the television off, and the father's expectation all support one compared-only claim about television sound and concentration.
relations.summary: Television sound is associated with poorer reading concentration, while reducing or removing it is expected to help.

relations.reason: The interruption incidents, successful phone separation, and stated experience jointly express one compared-only claim about notification control.
relations.summary: Nearby phone notifications interrupt note-taking and concentration, while placing the phone elsewhere prevents checking during reading.

relations.reason: The lost loose note and immediate resumption using the notebook jointly express one compared-only claim about dependable reading-place tracking.
relations.summary: Recording the page number in a notebook provided more reliable place-keeping than attaching a loose note to the book.

relations.reason: This is a compared-only limitation on the local agent's reading-related knowledge and prediction.
relations.summary: Past reading environments and interruptions can be summarized, but the next reading time cannot be predicted.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame covers reading-material placement, television and notification distractions, phone separation, reliable page tracking, and limits on predicting future reading times.
reports.reference_only: The reference covers medication timing and communication, appointment preparation, clinic seating, transportation support, and limits on inferring prescription status.
